data.exact_reserve_text: During 2015, net ultimate claims in respect of prior underwriting years (2014 & prior) increased by GBP 0.8m. This was mainly due to the Accident & Health class which saw an increase in exposure/written premium in the 2014 underwriting year. The General Liability and Offshore Energy classes also contributed to an increase in prior underwriting year net ultimate claims during 2015, as a result of large losses in these classes. These increases were more than offset by reductions due to favourable claims experience, most notably in Onshore Energy, but also Energy Casualty and Aerospace.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Increase in exposure / written premium in the 2014 underwriting year led to higher prior year ultimate claims for Accident & Health
Large losses in General Liability contributed to an increase in prior underwriting year ultimate claims
Offshore Energy large loss originating from the 2011 year of account contributed to prior year adverse development
Reductions due to favourable claims experience in Onshore Energy, Energy Casualty and Aerospace reduced prior year liabilities

data.standardized_narrative: Using the gross claims development triangle (gross of reinsurance) for underwriting years 2011-2013, there is a net favourable prior-year development of approximately GBP 10.3m (a release, -2.18% of opening gross claims outstanding). The report's narrative however states a net increase (net of reinsurance) of GBP 0.8m for prior underwriting years, driven by increased exposure in Accident & Health and large losses in General Liability and Offshore Energy, partly offset by favourable development in Onshore Energy, Energy Casualty and Aerospace. The extraction above is based on the gross triangle (preferred gross source) and therefore differs in sign and magnitude from the report's net figure because of reinsurance recoveries.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development gross figure was not explicitly stated in a "Movement in prior year's provision" note. Calculated gross prior year development from the gross claims development triangle (pages 37) for underwriting years <= 2013, giving a net release of ~GBP 10.323m. The report's narrative gives a net (after reinsurance) increase of GBP 0.8m; the difference is due to reinsurance recoveries. Gross triangle used as preferred gross source. Some LOB-level impacts are described qualitatively only; amounts by LOB are not quantified.
